compactMembership.notes: Wyoming's reciprocal-agreement network requires a separate application, fee, and Wyoming-issued license per applicant -- not a single multistate compact license practiced across member states without a new license. Recorded as false to avoid conflating the two mechanisms.

reciprocityRules.value: Wyoming's own official licensing page states: 'The State of Wyoming has a reciprocal Master Electrician license agreement with the following states: Idaho, South Dakota, and Iowa.' This Master-tier list is materially different from, and was verified independently of, the 17-state Journeyman list (see wyoming-journeyman.json) -- it is NOT assumed to carry the same conditions merely because Idaho, South Dakota, and Iowa also appear on the Journeyman list. To qualify for Master reciprocity, the applicant must have obtained their Master license from the named state by examination, with a score of 75% or greater (higher than Journeyman's 70% threshold), and have held it for at least 1 year from the date of examination, active and in good standing with no violations. Master reciprocity additionally requires the applicant to have held a Journeyman license for 4 years, with 8,000 hours of on-the-job training as a Journeyman Electrician and 4 years (576 hours) of apprenticeship schooling -- a prerequisite that does not apply to Journeyman-tier reciprocal applicants. Reciprocation into Wyoming is permitted only one (1) time -- if the reciprocated Wyoming license is allowed to lapse or expire, re-reciprocation is not permitted and the applicant must requalify by examination. Grandfathered origin-state licenses are not eligible. An applicant who has previously tested and failed a Wyoming Journeyman or Master exam is not eligible for a reciprocal license until they have held their primary-state license for 3 years. Unlike Oregon/Utah on the Journeyman list, no state-specific verification-letter carve-out was found for any Master-list state (Oregon and Utah do not appear on the Master list at all). This is a unidirectional statement of what Wyoming itself recognizes (State -> Wyoming); it does not establish that Idaho, South Dakota, or Iowa would in turn recognize a Wyoming Master license by reciprocity. Statutory basis: W.S. 35-9-126(d) authorizes the department to issue a reciprocal license where the applicant's out-of-state exam 'is equal to or exceeds' Wyoming's own exam -- the statute itself does not name any state, delegating that determination to the department; the 3-state list exists, as far as this research could establish, only on the department's webpage, not verbatim in the statute or the two administrative rule sections read (Wyo. Code R. 041-5 SS5-3 and SS5-5). Per the explicit strategic decision accompanying this research, Iowa's appearance here is recorded solely as a fact about Wyoming's own reciprocal list -- it is not, and should not be read as, an implementation of Iowa as its own electrician-state page (Iowa remains on HOLD).

reciprocityRules.notes: A third-party aggregator claim (not from any official Wyoming source, and not used as evidence) asserted Wyoming's reciprocal states are only 'Colorado, Montana, South Dakota, Utah, and Idaho' for 'active journeyman and master electricians' -- this directly contradicts the official page's own distinct 3-state Master list (which does not include Colorado, Montana, or Utah at all) and is recorded here only so it is not later mistaken for a superseding update.

endorsementRules.notes: Wyoming's own materials use the term 'reciprocal license' specifically, not 'endorsement' -- no separate endorsement pathway distinct from reciprocity was identified.

requiredExams.value: The examination is based on the current edition of the National Electrical Code (2023 NEC currently; 2026 NEC adopted effective 2026-07-01). A reciprocal applicant's origin-state Master exam must have been passed with a score of 75% or greater -- a higher threshold than Journeyman's 70%. Wyoming's own page states reciprocal licensure 'only exempts you from the exam not licensure requirements,' read here as meaning the Wyoming exam itself is waived for qualifying reciprocal applicants -- but this specific point could not be independently confirmed against a clean verbatim read of the codified rule text (Wyo. Code R. 041-5 SS5-5) and is flagged needs_review rather than silently resolved, exactly as for the Journeyman tier.

requiredExperience.value: Reciprocal applicants must still meet Wyoming's own underlying experience requirement: 8 years (16,000 hours) of work experience in the electrical wiring industry, of which 4 years (8,000 hours) must be documented as a licensed Journeyman, across residential, commercial, and industrial categories. Separately, the origin-state Master license itself must have been held for at least 1 year from the date of examination.

requiredDocuments.value: Government-issued ID (driver's license, state ID, or passport); current Master license card from the reciprocating state; apprenticeship/education transcript documenting the Journeyman-history prerequisite; a unique personal email address; CEU certificates documenting 16 hours (>=8 code-related) completed within the 3 years since the applicant's last license renewal. No state-specific verification-letter carve-out (like Oregon/Utah on the Journeyman list) was found for any Master-list state.
